findings.text: the guard pins the relevance registry as disjoint from CODE_RESET_SPECS['triaged'].clear_fields, but a file reset to 'triaged' from 'scored'/'ingested' keeps relevance_stage='content' while _CODE_SCORE_FIELDS clears score_composite, so it satisfies neither the enrichment claim (needs relevance_stage='name' and score_composite >= threshold, graph_ops.py:420) nor the triage claim (needs status='discovered' and relevance_stage IS NULL, graph_ops.py:322) nor the score claim (needs is_enriched=true, graph_ops.py:507); reset-to-triaged appears to leave a file claimed by nothing. The clear lists predate this node (unchanged in diff 8e08eeaa7..156d39a1f), so this is a pre-existing coherence gap the node's new assertion now codifies rather than an introduction; the plan does not settle reset-to-triaged semantics.

set(scorer.RELEVANCE_FIELDS) == set(reset_module.CODE_RELEVANCE_FIELDS) cannot fail: scorer.RELEVANCE_FIELDS is the same tuple object imported from reset (scorer.py:33-35), so this assertion adds no drift guard beyond the meaningful subset/isdisjoint checks above it. The real drift guard is the import-time KeyError in _relevance_field (scorer.py:66-70), which does fire on an unregistered field.

after_suite.revision is f4c0df4f9 and baseline_suite.revision is 3d470b24e, neither of which is the reviewed head 156d39a1f nor the run's declared orientation_base_* (base_sha 8e08eeaa7).
